methodology: Private static review of saved keyboard focus hooks, accessible status elements, pagination observers and page-level request completion announcements. Publishes only capture-local file ordinals and authored analysis.

mechanisms.description: An exported client component places a visually hidden focusable heading immediately before the composer with an accessible latest-response label; a matching page import supplies its navigate callback.
A document keydown listener and footer focusin listener adjust the landmark's tabIndex to avoid trapping normal tab movement, while allowing focus to become available after footer navigation.
Focusing the heading aborts any earlier navigation, calls the provided async target resolver and, if the heading remains focused and a target exists, focuses that target without scrolling.
When the target resolver reports no available response, the component publishes a screen-reader-only status explaining that no latest response is available.

The conversation's older-message sentinel uses IntersectionObserver against the thread scroll root and can request older content when the sentinel intersects; a loaded or exhausted history state suppresses it.
The older-message sentinel renders a retry control when loading failed; otherwise it renders a loading spinner with a screen-reader-only loading label inside a status role.

A page-level hook keeps a visually hidden, atomic polite-live status in a portal. It records active request identity while streaming, clears the announcement during a response, and reports completion only when matching request state is complete and not otherwise suppressed.
A conversation loading surface exposes an aria-busy status region with an accessible label while the relevant page view is waiting for conversation data.

limits: A source-level aria-live or role attribute is not evidence that a specific assistive technology spoke the text.
A focus-navigation callback can be aborted, fail to find a target or depend on virtual row materialization; successful keyboard navigation was not observed.
History fetching and pagination are conditional on cursor, errors, viewport state and network; no real request was observed.
The study does not assess WCAG conformance, focus restoration quality, screen-reader traversal of unmounted turns, or live behavior in a deployed browser.
privacy: No user text, account identifiers, original archive resource names, JavaScript snippets, network endpoints or runtime session state published.
